name: @projexlight/service-pool-federation-runtime
summary: Cross-pool federation runtime (G10 closer) — discovery + health probing + routing for per-tenant + per-app pool families. Maintains the live pool topology so sdk-pool-router can resolve a tenant request to the right pool in O(1). Active-active failover engagement lives here.

events.name: pool-federation.topology.changed.v1
events.description: Pool topology mutation (attach / detach / region change).

events.name: pool-federation.health.degraded.v1
events.description: Pool health probe crossed degraded threshold.

events.name: pool-federation.failover.engaged.v1
events.description: Active-active failover engaged; partner region takes traffic.

hooks.name: registerPool
hooks.description: Register a new pool into the federation topology.

hooks.name: probeHealth
hooks.description: On-demand health probe; usually run by the periodic prober.

hooks.name: engageFailover
hooks.description: Operator-driven (or auto-policy) failover to a partner region.

hooks.name: startProber
hooks.description: Background worker — probes every pool on the configured cadence.

scenarios.title: Add a new EU app pool to the federation
scenarios.when_to_use: Scale-out — capacity team brings up a new EU pool; register it so pool-router can route EU tenants to it.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Pool registered; topology event emitted. lineage-projector backfills the new pool's lineage. pool-router starts routing eligible tenants.

scenarios.title: Pool degraded → traffic shifts away
scenarios.when_to_use: Probe detects elevated latency / error rate; emit .health.degraded.v1; pool-router de-weights the pool until recovery.
scenarios.example_code:
// driven by startProber on cadence;
// emits when p95 > POOL_FEDERATION_DEGRADED_THRESHOLD_MS for N consecutive probes.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Traffic gradually shifts to healthy peers. Recovery flips weight back.

scenarios.title: Region-level failover
scenarios.when_to_use: Tier-G+ — partner region is healthy + home is degraded; engageFailover atomically points DNS + pool-router to the partner.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Failover engaged within ~60s (RTO target). Audit chain pins reason + persona who engaged. Sync-replicated SDKs (audit, payment) continue serving; async SDKs flush their tail.

scenarios.title: Drain + remove an old pool
scenarios.when_to_use: Capacity team wants to retire an old pool; drain stops new tenants + lets existing finish.
scenarios.example_code:
import { deregisterPool } from '@projexlight/service-pool-federation-runtime';
await deregisterPool({ pool_index: 'us-east-app-1', drain_hours: 24 });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Pool drained, then removed. Existing tenants migrated to peers.

scenarios.title: Monthly active-active failover drill
scenarios.when_to_use: Required for Tier-G+ SLO — monthly drill to prove failover works.
scenarios.example_code: // run via scheduled job; engageFailover + immediately revert.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Drill emits the same audit events as a real failover. SLO clock records drill duration.

compliance_posture.notes: Region pinning enforces residency — a tenant pinned to EU never has its requests federated to a US pool. Failover events satisfy SOC2-CC7.4 evidence; monthly drills satisfy the FedRAMP CP-9 contingency plan requirement.
